description.narrative:
Sri Lanka has recorded a steady economic growth of 5% per annum for the past decade. In 2019, it attained an upper middle-income country status with a per capita income of $4,020. To continue achieving higher incomes and better standards of living, the government commits to becoming a knowledge-based economy by 2025. Investments in human capital and education have been prioritized for economic diversification and enhanced productivity.
Alignment with country strategy and ADB's value addition: SESIP is aligned with ADB's Strategy 2030, ADB's Country Partnership Strategy 2018-2022 and contributes to pillar 1 (promoting economic diversification and productivity enhancement) by upgrading human capital. It is included in the ADB's Country Operations Business Plan 2020-2022. Although SESIP financing represents only 3.4% of government secondary education spending, it aims to bring transformational change to secondary education and will add value by (i) supporting integrated reforms in curriculum, pedagogy, and assessment that will influence the overall education sector; (ii) training teachers with innovative training modalities that will impact on both pre-service and in-service teacher training quality and modalities; and (iii) focusing efforts at the school level with dedicated resources to improve learning outcomes of the underperforming rural school students. ADB's extensive engagement and experience in implementing similar reforms in several other Asian countries can be utilized. ADB is a long-term, trusted partner of Sri Lanka in secondary education and skills development and has ongoing projects in skills development and higher education, where strong synergy with secondary education will be sought.
SESIP will support the government's secondary education sub-sector program, expected to cost $5.80 billion from 2020 to 2025. ADB will finance $195 million for the RBL and $5 million for the associated project loan, with the balance to be funded by the government. The program expenditure framework and financing plan is in Appendix 4. Considering the ongoing efforts being made by the government in preparing SESIP, financing for prior results may be considered in areas that are integral to curriculum and pedagogical reform -- central to the success of reform implementation.
The RBL program and the associated project loan will be implemented from May 2020 to December 2025. The MOE will be the executing agency for both RBL and investment project. A SESIP steering committee will be established, comprising MOE, National Education Commission, National Institute of Education, Department of Examinations, Provincial Council, Finance Commission, and PEAs and other key stakeholders. The steering committee will be headed by Secretary, MOE. A SESIP program unit will be established within MOE to coordinate and monitor the progress in achieving the DLIs as well as implement and monitor the procurement of consulting services under the investment project. Procurement for the associated project loan will be undertaken following the ADB Procurement Policy: Goods, Works, Non-consulting and Consulting Services (2017, as amended from time to time); and the ADB Procurement Regulations for ADB Borrowers: Goods, Works, Non-consulting and Consulting Services (2017, as amended from time to time).

Output: Quality and relevance of secondary science, technology, mathematics, and commerce programs enhanced. Indicator: At least 65% of grades 10-12 teachers in ‘O' and ‘A' Level program-targeted subjects implement inquiry-based and interactive teaching practices by online and distance learning, and face-to-face classroom instruction (at least 60% women trainees). Progress/Status: 1.b. MOE and NIE have undertaken a full review and alignment of the NEPF with the NTSF. ADB TA has observed and provided feedback on the teacher training programs conducted by NIE for teachers of the piloting programs. The criteria and/or minimum standards for the applied resource hubs (ARHs) for teacher training in new pedagogy have been approved, equipment ordering has begun, and procurement is ongoing. Teacher training modules for target subjects in O/L (grades 10 & 11) have been developed, including training modules, video programs, and sample training activities for online teacher training. The Training of Trainers (TOT) program for 50% of the staff and a resource pool of national ARHs have been completed.
Data Source: MOE and NIE information systems; and evaluation reports against school education quality index and checklists Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2025 Target value: Y

Output: Sector management capacity strengthened. Indicator: By 2025, all key sector indicators, including sex-disaggregated data, from MOE, NIE, and DOE made publicly available on the MOE website and published as annual sector performance reports Progress/Status: 3.a. The development of the national M&E framework involved several drafts and consultations with all stakeholders (MOE, NIE, DOE, and nine PEAs). The alignment of the M&E framework with the National Education Policy Framework (NEPF) has been completed by introducing necessary changes to the KPIs and introducing sub-indicators. Due to administrative reasons and delays in the recruitment of NEMIS software developers, the sub-DLI progress was slow. It is expected that the Data Management Branch (DMB) will obtain the necessary technical personnel to complete the development of NEMIS and make it fully functional by the end of 2024.
Data Source: MOE information systems, and annual sector performance report Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2025 Target value: Y
Secondary education system transformed and aligned with evolving labor force needs.

21st century skills (problem solving, creative thinking, teamwork, and communication) satisfactorily applied and implemented in new curriculum, pedagogy, and assessment system Achievement: Y Progress/Status: (i) National Curriculum Framework (NCF) developed & approved; and (ii) Modular-based curricula for subjects are being prepared. Curriculum, pedagogy, and assessment system is being developed, i.e. O/L Maths and Science, and grade 12 A/L STMC curricula, instructional materials have been developed. Development of grade 13 SMTC curricula and instructional materials is in progress. Training of teachers is underway on newly developed O/L curricula and materials. The implementation of the program (proposed reforms under ESDP 2020-2025) was suspended by the government due to the decision of the cabinet of ministers to review the new education reforms together with the newly developed “National Education Policy 2020-2030” prepared by NEC. The expert committee to assist the cabinet subcommittee has submitted the draft NEPF to the president's office. The cabinet approval was received and MoE/NIE started the implementation with plan to rollout the new curriculum in 2026 for grades 1,6, and 10. However, the new government requested to do a proper pilot in 2025 and suggested to start the rollout in 2026. With this decision, the program timeframe needs to be revised and it will affect for the projected disbursements as well. Data Source: Evaluation report; MOE, NIE records, and DOE public reports; interviews Base year: 2019 Baseline value: N
